title: Ancient Bengal and Urban Civilization
tagline: Early cities, Gauda power, Pala institutions, and the Sena transition
intro: Read ancient and early medieval Bengal through archaeology, regional kingdoms, Buddhist monastic centers, and late pre-Sultanate political change.
description: A foundation hub linking Mahasthangarh, Shashanka’s Gauda, Pala-Sena state formation, Somapura Mahavihara, and the transition toward Turko-Afghan conquest.
seoTitle: Ancient and Early Medieval Bengal: Mahasthangarh, Gauda, Pala and Sena History
seoDescription: Explore ancient and early medieval Bengal through Mahasthangarh, Shashanka, the Pala dynasty, Somapura Mahavihara, Sena rule, figures, sources, and learning paths.
beginnerSummary: Start here to understand Bengal before the Sultanate: urban sites, early kingship, Buddhist learning, and the Sena-era political transition.
advancedSummary: Compare archaeological evidence, dynastic narratives, religious patronage, and regional power formation before the 1204-1205 conquest.

faq.question: Why begin with Mahasthangarh?
faq.answer: Mahasthangarh anchors the hub in archaeological evidence for early urban and administrative life in Bengal before later dynastic histories.

faq.question: How do the Pala and Sena periods connect?
faq.answer: The Pala period highlights Buddhist institutional patronage and regional kingship, while the Sena transition shows changing elite power before Turko-Afghan conquest.

faq.question: Which sources are best for this topic?
faq.answer: Use archaeological references for Mahasthangarh and Somapura alongside regional histories of the Pala and Sena dynasties.

learningPath.reason: Place the topic in period context.
